pages.text: The $(item)WEFAX$() program receives weather fax charts through a radio interface cabled to the computer: charts other stations send, the solar bulletins and blackout alerts of $(l:radiocraft:sky/ionosphere)Ionospheric Processors$(), and on request (F4, WX REPT) the coast station's broadcast, the radar chart and then the forecast, as the $(l:radiocraft:sky/wefax)WEFAX receiver$() prints them. WX REPT needs a radio with a real antenna.

Charts come in line by line, speckled where the signal was lost, and are kept on the disk ($(thing)WFX00001.IMG$()).$(br2)F7 draws a chart of the weather where the computer is (radar or forecast); F3 sends any picture as a chart, in greys, as long on the air as a fax sheet. WEFAX receivers with AUTO on start printing when they hear one.
A blank floppy and an empty map.
